alloy.preparation: Cast stainless steel. The exact thermal and surface preparation of the Figure 9 pitting specimen is not separately specified; heat treatments attached to other polarization figures are not assigned.
alloy.microstructure: Stable austenitic cast stainless steel; a small amount of stable ferrite may be present.

test_method.procedure_description: Wenking potentiostat with stepping-motor potential progression maintained at the printed stepping rate of 10 mV/min; polarization cell/electrode holder as recommended by Greene and polarization according to ASTM G.1 Committee recommendations. All potentials referred to the paper’s S.C.E. calomel scale. Figure 9 specifies 30°C and N2 purge in 3% NaCl. No individual potential increment or step-hold duration is supplied.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Authors’ explicitly stated breakdown/pitting potential in the chloride polarization test; no numerical onset-current threshold is specified.

experiments.result_note: Explicit text-reported pitting/breakdown potential. All potentials are stated relative to S.C.E.; no threshold was independently inferred from a continuous curve. Composition is nominal percent, not a recovered full chemical analysis; no Fe balance or unstated elements are calculated. No solvent, pH, chloride-ion concentration or concentration basis is inferred from “3% NaCl”.

experiments.result_note: Explicit text-reported pitting/breakdown potential. All potentials are stated relative to S.C.E.; no threshold was independently inferred from a continuous curve. Approximately +800 mV, as qualified by the source. Composition is nominal percent, not a recovered full chemical analysis; no Fe balance or unstated elements are calculated. No solvent, pH, chloride-ion concentration or concentration basis is inferred from “3% NaCl”. The final nominal FERRALIUM composition (25% Cr, 5.5% Ni, 3% Cu, 2.5% Mo) is explicitly listed on PDF p.5; the earlier 25Cr/5Ni/3Mo discussion describes development steps. The separate Figure 17 solution treatment at 1120°C and subsequent 500°C aging do not identify the precise Figure 11 specimen treatment.
